chunks: He said: And al-Rida (peace be upon him) said, regarding the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'It is He who shows you the lightning in fear and in hope' [13:12]. He said: Fear for the traveller, and hope for the settler.

key_terms.البرق: Lightning — a natural phenomenon cited in the Quran as a sign of God's power
key_terms.المسافر: The traveller — one who is on a journey, vulnerable to storms
key_terms.المقيم: The settler/resident — one who stays in place, benefits from rainfall

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Rida explain the fear and hope mentioned with lightning in the Quran?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) provides a practical interpretation of Quran 13:12, which describes lightning as causing both fear and hope. The Imam explains that the fear is for the traveller (who faces danger from storms on the road) while the hope is for the settler (who anticipates the rain that lightning heralds for agriculture). This interpretation, part of the seventeenth assembly's series of Quranic commentaries, demonstrates the Imam's attention to the lived experience of different groups in understanding divine signs.
